# Provisional hypothesis: discordant renal recovery after acute kidney injury

## Proposed relationship
Among adults with an acute kidney injury (AKI) episode in MIMIC-IV, patients whose creatinine has returned toward baseline but whose urine output and/or fluid balance remain abnormal at a prespecified 48-hour assessment will have a higher risk of subsequent in-hospital death or persistent/recurrent kidney dysfunction than patients with concordant creatinine and urine-output recovery, after accounting for baseline illness severity and treatment context.

This is a hypothesis, not an observed result. The clinical opening is that creatinine-based recovery may be a misleading surrogate: creatinine can fall because of dilution, altered production, or recovery while residual tubular dysfunction or fluid overload persists. Resolving this would clarify whether a single creatinine criterion is sufficient for judging renal recovery and for deciding whether continued monitoring or renal-risk assessment is warranted.

- The expert seed `expert-20260913-mimic-03` (candidate `candidate-209a992a877034bf9d300fd7`) explicitly proposes that creatinine falling without improvement in urine output or fluid status leaves patients at high risk, and identifies the limitation that measured kidney function is unavailable.

# HCC early liver-directed treatment and 1-year mortality: working proposal

## Scientific opening and unresolved question
The configured HCC data contain many patients with liver-cancer diagnoses and repeated encounters, procedures, medications, examinations, and clinical documents. A recorded liver-directed intervention may be associated with survival, but the clinically important uncertainty is whether that association reflects treatment benefit or competing explanations: patients selected for treatment may have different tumor burden/stage, liver reserve, performance status, access, or documentation intensity; and survival follow-up may be incomplete or informative.

The provisional hypothesis is: among adults with a first documented HCC diagnosis in the HCC dataset, receiving a recorded liver-directed treatment during the early post-index interval is associated with lower 1-year all-cause mortality than no recorded treatment, after adjustment for baseline age, sex, comorbidity burden, disease stage/extent when documented, and treatment-selection proxies. This is an observational treatment-association hypothesis, not a causal treatment-benefit claim.

The leading rival explanations are (1) stage and tumor burden: earlier or less extensive disease is more likely to receive treatment and has better prognosis; (2) selection/healthcare access: treatment receipt reflects availability, performance status, and clinician judgment; (3) documentation intensity: more observed encounters produce more recorded procedures and more complete follow-up; and (4) informative censoring: patients with sparse follow-up may appear to survive or die differently. A treatment association that disappears after stage/selection adjustment, or is concentrated among patients with dense documentation, supports a rival explanation rather than treatment benefit.

If the diagnosis table has no timestamp, the encounter time is the operational index time; this limitation must be reported.

Primary treatment definition: a procedure row in `procedures` with `开始时间` from index time through index time + 30 days and a prespecified liver-directed label set. The label set is to be frozen after a bounded review of the observed procedure vocabulary; initial candidates are TACE/embolization (`TACE`, `经导管肝动脉栓塞术`, `动脉化疗栓塞`, `经动脉造影化疗栓塞术（TACE）`), hepatic resection (`肝叶切除术`, `肝叶部分切除术`, `腹腔镜下肝部分切除术`, `部分肝切除术`, `特殊肝段切除术`), and ablation (`微波消融`, `射频消融`). `TACE` and its variants are not to be double-counted as separate modalities. A secondary definition adds systemic therapy from `medications` only after a prespecified drug-name mapping is reviewed; it is not mixed into the primary definition.

Patients with a qualifying procedure before index time are excluded from the primary incident-treatment cohort, with a sensitivity analysis retaining them and labeling prior treatment. Patients with no qualifying procedure through 30 days are the untreated comparator. Treatment is time-zero exposure, not a time-varying exposure, to avoid post-index outcome conditioning.

## Covariates, outcome, and follow-up
Baseline covariates are measured or derived from records dated at or before index time: age and sex from `encounters`; department from `encounters.就诊科室`; comorbidity indicators from pre-index `diagnoses`; liver disease indicators from pre-index diagnoses (`肝硬化`, `乙肝后肝硬化`, `门静脉高压`, `门静脉瘤栓`, etc.); baseline laboratory values from `labs` using the last valid result in a prespecified 30-day pre-index window, with missingness indicators; imaging/examination count and stage-related text features from `examinations`; and documentation density from the number of encounters, diagnoses, labs, examinations, and orders before index. Stage is a primary covariate only when extractable from diagnosis labels or adjudicated text; otherwise it is an uncertainty, not silently imputed as known.

The primary outcome is all-cause mortality within 365 days of index time. Because the catalog has no explicit death table, mortality must be operationalized as an in-hospital death outcome only if a death field is found and validated in the source rows; otherwise the primary outcome is unavailable and the study must not claim 1-year mortality. The fallback computable endpoint is 1-year observed survival/contact status using the last documented HCC encounter (`出院时间`/`就诊时间`) as administrative censoring, explicitly labeled as informative and not equivalent to mortality. A second analysis may use death recorded in clinical documents or diagnoses only after prespecified text adjudication; this requires expert review.

Follow-up is from index time to the earliest of 365 days, validated death, or last documented contact. Patients with no later encounter are censored at last contact, not assumed alive. Report the proportion with follow-up beyond 30, 90, and 365 days, and perform inverse-probability-of-censoring sensitivity analysis. The key limitation is that this dataset may not contain reliable external mortality capture; any mortality conclusion is conditional on the operational endpoint and must state that limitation.

## Baseline and substantive alternative
The simple baseline is a prespecified cause-specific or fine-Gray model for the operational 1-year endpoint, with treatment as the exposure and a transparent adjustment set: age, sex, index department, comorbidity/liver-disease indicators, documented stage, baseline laboratory values, and documentation density. Report standardized mortality/contact risk differences and 95% confidence intervals, with missing-stage and missing-lab sensitivity analyses. This baseline tests the adjusted association but loses nonlinear interactions, time-varying observation processes, and the distinction between treatment assignment and treatment effect.

The substantive alternative is a two-part selection/observation model: (i) estimate treatment propensity from baseline covariates and documentation intensity, and (ii) estimate the outcome and censoring models, then compare standardized risks under the treated and untreated exposure distributions using inverse-probability weighting or g-computation, with overlap diagnostics and a prespecified positivity threshold. A secondary learned model (gradient-boosted survival model or regularized cause-specific model) can use the same baseline inputs and predict the endpoint, but it is evaluated for calibration, discrimination, and treatment-effect stability—not rewarded for a small predictive gain. The alternative reveals whether the association is concentrated in a selected treatment region, whether documentation intensity explains it, and whether nonlinear stage/liver-reserve interactions change the adjusted estimate. It does not identify a causal mechanism.

Both methods use the same patient-level split (e.g., 70/30 by `患者主索引`, with no patient appearing in both train and test), the same endpoint, and the same uncertainty evaluation (bootstrap or cluster-robust confidence intervals; calibration plots; standardized risk differences). The baseline is selected as the primary interpretable analysis; the learned/selection model is retained because it tests the clinically important selection and documentation rivals. A GPU is not required for these tabular analyses; CPU is adequate unless the learned model is expanded, in which case a bounded allocated probe should verify runtime.

## Falsification and interpretation
Pre-specify these checks before fitting: (1) treatment labels recorded after index but before the 30-day window are excluded from exposure and used as a timing/negative-control check; (2) a pseudo-treatment date shifted outside the early window should not reproduce the association; (3) exclude patients with no post-index contact and compare with censoring-weighted results; (4) stratify by documented stage and documentation density; (5) compare procedure-only and procedure-plus-medication definitions; (6) assess positivity, missingness, and calibration. A supportive result requires a reproducible adjusted risk difference with adequate overlap and robustness to stage/missingness and censoring checks. An adverse result is no association, reversal, or disappearance after stage/documentation adjustment, which supports selection or documentation explanations. An inconclusive result is sparse treatment, poor stage coverage, inadequate follow-up, or wide intervals; it does not refute benefit.

No result from these observational analyses establishes that treatment causes survival benefit. Establishing causal benefit would require a validated mortality registry, reliable treatment assignment/intent, clinical adjudication of stage and performance status, and preferably a prospective or quasi-experimental design. The actual deliverable is a newly fitted, uncertainty-quantified treatment-association analysis with exact cohort construction, endpoint limitations, and rival-explanation diagnostics.

## Evidence status and next steps
The dataset headers and representative rows were inspected, and the diagnosis/procedure vocabulary was scanned. The key remaining checks are: validate whether any death/mortality field exists in the HCC source rows; freeze the procedure label map and stage extraction; quantify index-cohort size, treatment coverage, follow-up, and missingness; and inspect three hypothesis-specific public works with frozen receipts. No effect estimate or clinical conclusion is claimed yet.

# Repaired hypothesis: discordant renal recovery after AKI

## Scientific question and clinical importance

Among adults with an ICU stay and a documented acute kidney injury (AKI), does a creatinine trajectory that appears to improve while urine output and/or fluid balance remain abnormal identify higher subsequent risk than concordant recovery? This matters because a creatinine-only recovery assessment may miss residual renal dysfunction or fluid accumulation and could misguide monitoring and renal-risk decisions.

The expert seed `expert-20260913-mimic-03` proposes this question. It is an untested opening, not evidence for the association. The closest inspected evidence is that creatinine can overestimate kidney function after prolonged critical illness [K1], that urine-output criteria can identify AKI earlier than creatinine criteria in a selected cardiac-surgery setting [K2], and that KDIGO defines AKI using both creatinine and urine-output criteria [K3]. None establishes that discordant recovery after a fixed landmark predicts later outcomes.

## Hypothesis and rival explanation

Hypothesis: at a prespecified 48-hour post-AKI landmark, patients with creatinine recovery but persistent oliguria and/or positive fluid balance have higher risk of subsequent in-hospital death or a new kidney-replacement event than patients with concordant recovery, after adjustment for baseline illness severity and treatment context.

The strongest rival is that discordance is a marker of severity, observation intensity, diuretics, dialysis, or documentation rather than residual renal dysfunction. The experiment must therefore compare adjusted associations, repeat analyses with alternative AKI definitions and measurement windows, and explicitly treat a null/reversal as evidence against using this discordance as a risk marker. This is prognostic, not causal.

## Population and temporal design

Use one first qualifying ICU stay per patient in MIMIC-IV 3.1. Include adults (anchor_age >=18; ages >89 are represented as 91) with a valid `icu/icustays.intime`, a creatinine measurement in `hosp/labevents` during the ICU stay, and at least 48 hours of observation after the AKI landmark. Exclude stays with a missing or non-numeric creatinine at the landmark or with a creatinine measurement after the landmark that is used to define the exposure.

Define AKI onset as the earliest creatinine time satisfying either (a) an increase of >=0.3 mg/dL from the earliest prior creatinine within the preceding 48 hours, or (b) an increase to >=1.5 times the earliest prior creatinine within the preceding 7 days. If no prior creatinine exists, use the first creatinine >=1.5 mg/dL as a secondary prespecified proxy and report it separately. The primary AKI definition is the creatinine criterion; urine-output-only AKI is a sensitivity analysis because the ICU stay may begin after the urine-output event. Set the landmark to 48 hours after AKI onset. Require a creatinine measurement within +/-12 hours of the landmark and a urine-output record in the preceding 24 hours. Follow-up begins at the landmark and ends at hospital discharge, death, or 7 days, whichever occurs first.

## Exposure, outcome and variables

Creatinine recovery is defined as landmark creatinine <= baseline creatinine +0.3 mg/dL and <=1.2 times baseline, using the earliest qualifying prior creatinine as baseline. Urine-output recovery is >=0.5 mL/kg/hour over the 24-hour window before the landmark, using `icu/inputevents.patientweight` when available and otherwise a prespecified imputation/missingness analysis. Fluid-balance abnormality is positive net balance over the same 24-hour window: sum of `icu/inputevents.amount` for `Fluids/Intake` items minus sum of `icu/outputevents.value` for urine items, with unit conversion to mL. The primary discordance group is creatinine recovery plus either urine-output non-recovery or positive fluid balance. The concordant reference group has creatinine recovery, urine-output recovery, and non-positive fluid balance. A secondary exposure contrasts creatinine non-recovery with recovery while stratifying by urine/fluid status.

Primary outcome is in-hospital death after the landmark, from `hosp/admissions.deathtime` and `hospital_expire_flag`. Secondary outcome is a new kidney-replacement event after the landmark, identified from `icu/procedureevents` dialysis/CRRT procedure items (including item IDs 225441, 225802, 225803, 225805, 225809 and 225810) or `hosp/procedures_icd` dialysis procedures; report item-level adjudication and exclude events already present before the landmark. Persistent/recurrent creatinine elevation is an exploratory endpoint, not a substitute for measured kidney function.

Covariates are age, gender, admission type/location, ICU care unit, landmark creatinine, baseline-to-landmark creatinine change, SOFA or APACHE components available from `icu/chartevents` and `hosp/labevents`, vasopressor exposure, diuretic exposure, dialysis before landmark, and missingness indicators. # MerTK-dependent macrophage–fibroblast context hypothesis

Seed D2-T1; parent candidate-674d76d0840c113916e011b8. This is a planned hypothesis, not an executed result.

## Question and clinical importance

In RA synovium, reciprocal macrophage–fibroblast signaling is proposed to sustain a failed-resolution state [K1]. The unresolved question is whether an intervention-associated transcriptional response in fibroblast-like synoviocytes (FLS) depends on the identity of the macrophage partner, and whether that dependence is selectively altered when MerTK signaling is perturbed. This matters because a target that changes only a subset of macrophage–fibroblast contexts would predict selective rather than universal therapeutic effects; it also distinguishes a context-gated response from a generic inflammatory response.

The strongest evidence currently supports only that the available experiments contain matched macrophage–FLS co-culture conditions and MerTK-inhibitor perturbations, and that MerTK/CD206-positive and negative macrophage populations are experimentally represented. It does not establish that the inhibitor acts directly on MerTK in every cell, that transcriptional changes are causal, or that a clinical treatment effect exists.

## Hypothesis

Among FLS co-cultured with macrophages, the intervention-associated transcriptional response will be larger and more reproducible in the MerTK/CD206-positive macrophage context than in the MerTK/CD206-negative context, and the difference will be attenuated by MerTK inhibition. The primary estimand is the context-by-intervention interaction in log2 fold change of FLS transcript abundance, not a claim of direct MerTK target action.

A falsifiable prediction is that the interaction contrast
(response in Mpos context - response in Mneg context)
is positive for a prespecified inflammatory/activation response and decreases toward zero after MerTK inhibition. A secondary prediction is that the interaction is not explained by a generic LPS effect: the same direction should not appear in FLS-only controls.

## Exact data and contrasts

E-MTAB-8873 is the primary targeted single-cell assay. Use the read-only source matrices and SDRF under:
[private-path]/E-MTAB-8873
The registry identifies 445 measured feature columns (446 including Cell_Index) and source names such as R1_SA256A_FLS_only, R1_SA256A_FLS_SA259A_Mpos, R1_SA256A_FLS_SA259A_Mneg, R1_SA256A_FLS_SA259A_Mpos_Inhibitor, and R1_SA256A_FLS_SA259A_Mneg_Inhibitor. The SDRF fields are Source Name, Characteristics[cell type], Characteristics[stimulus], Characteristics[disease], Characteristics[individual], Factor Value[growth condition], Factor Value[stimulus], and Derived Array Data File. The matrix rows are Cell_Index; feature columns retain identifiers such as MERTK|NM_006343.2|Reference_end, CD209|NM_021155.3|Reference_end, ARG1|NM_000045.3|Reference_end, TGFB1|NM_000660.5|PolyA_1, SPP1|NM_000582.2|Reference_end, and TNF|NM_000594.3|Reference_end.

For each recorded FLS/co-culture sample, summarize the targeted panel to a pseudobulk mean per cell index after retaining only live-cell rows defined by the assay registry/protocol; do not treat technical replicates as independent donors. The primary paired comparison is within the same FLS donor and macrophage partner where both Mpos and Mneg conditions exist. The intervention contrast is Inhibitor - corresponding untreated condition for the same partner context, using only explicitly matched source pairs. The context contrast is Mpos - Mneg within FLS donor. The interaction is (Inhibitor-Mpos) - (Inhibitor-Mneg) expressed on the log scale of pseudobulk expression, with the FLS-only source as a negative control. If a source lacks a matched pair, it is excluded from the paired estimand and reported, not imputed as independent evidence.

E-MTAB-8316 is a secondary bulk RNA-seq context check, not a replacement for the targeted assay. Its read-only matrix is [private-path]/MK_readcountMatrix.txt.gz, with 12 condition samples and 13 columns (Geneid plus MK3, MK4, MK7, MK8, MK11, MK12, MK15, MK16, MK19, MK20, MK23, MK24). The SDRF binds Source Name, Characteristics[cell type], Characteristics[stimulus], Characteristics[individual], Characteristics[specimen], Factor Value[compound], Factor Value[dose], and Derived Array Data File. The protocol records LPS-stimulated macrophages and UNC106238 at 250 micromolar in the inhibitor samples. Use the six donor/specimen pairs as repeated context measurements, average replicate rows within donor/condition before inference, and do not call them twelve independent donors. This dataset is not a targeted panel and cannot establish cell-specific expression unless the metadata and protocol are reconciled.

## Baseline and substantive alternative

Baseline: a prespecified donor-aware paired analysis of the targeted panel. For each gene, calculate log2 pseudobulk fold changes for the intervention and context contrasts, then estimate the interaction with a linear model with donor as the repeated unit and FLS-only control as an offset/negative control. Use permutation within donor and a false-discovery-rate threshold; report effect sizes and uncertainty, not only significance.

Substantive alternative: a joint hierarchical interaction model across the measured FLS–macrophage context pairs, with donor and partner-context random effects, gene-specific context slopes, and a shared inflammatory response factor estimated from the prespecified panel. Fit the model to the same E-MTAB-8873 pseudobulk inputs and evaluate by donor-held-out prediction of the context-by-inhibitor contrast and by calibration of the interaction posterior/credible intervals. The alternative can reveal whether a coherent context-gated program is shared across donors and whether the apparent interaction is driven by one donor or one partner; the baseline loses that structure and may overstate isolated gene effects. If the hierarchical model is unstable because of the small donor count, defer it and retain the baseline as the primary result.

## Outcomes and interpretation

Supportive: a reproducible positive context-by-inhibitor interaction in the targeted assay, with FLS-only controls near null, uncertainty excluding the prespecified effect region, and consistency in the E-MTAB-8316 bulk check. This would support context-dependent intervention-associated transcription and justify a perturbation study, but not direct MerTK causality.

Adverse: no interaction, an interaction of opposite sign, or a large FLS-only control effect. This would argue against the proposed context gate or indicate that the observed change is generic to LPS/inhibitor exposure, donor selection, or measurement.

Inconclusive: wide intervals, failed matched-pair availability, unstable hierarchical fitting, or discordant assays. This would not refute the hypothesis; it would identify the need for more donors, better matched conditions, or direct target validation.

## Limits and next test

The data contain intervention-associated transcription, not proof that UNC106238 directly blocks MerTK in the relevant cells, not clinical outcomes, and not whole-tissue or complete transcriptome coverage. The next test is a donor-matched perturbation with direct MerTK engagement readout (for example, validated target occupancy/phosphorylation or a genetic MerTK perturbation), paired with the same FLS-only and macrophage-context controls. Clinical relevance would additionally require patient-level outcomes or expert adjudication of synovial disease state.

# Early menopause and cardiac structure in UK Biobank: a bounded exploratory hypothesis

## Scientific question and claim
Among women reporting natural menopause, is earlier age at menopause associated with greater cardiac structural change at the assessment, after accounting for age, body size, blood pressure, smoking, and HRT timing? The strongest existing evidence supports an observational association between early menopause and cardiovascular events, but does not establish a causal hormonal mechanism; a recent MR review found no significant causal association for coronary heart disease or stroke. The unresolved claim here is narrower: whether the association is present in measured LV/LA structure and persists after measured cardiovascular load adjustment.

## Population and time
Use UKB `ukb672073` participants with sex=2, field 2724=1 (had natural menopause), and positive field 3581 (age at last menstrual period). Restrict to baseline assessment instance 0 for the primary cross-sectional association; do not use instance 3 as follow-up because the available MRI instance timing is not sufficient to establish a prospective change. Follow-up events are secondary and exploratory only. The assessment date is field 53-0.0; field 53-1.0 is available for a repeat-measurement sensitivity analysis but only 20,343 rows have it in the completed subset.

## Exact data bindings
All joins use `eid` within the `ukb672073` identifier namespace. Source snapshot is `ukb-completed-subset-20261002`.
- Assessment table: `[private-path]/ukb_d61ec821b81b9034.parquet`, source `ukb_d61ec821b81b9034_parquet`, 502,370 rows. Required columns: `eid`, `31-0.0` (sex), `53-0.0`/`53-1.0` (assessment dates), `2724-0.0` (had menopause), `3581-0.0` (age at menopause), `3536-0.0`/`3546-0.0` (HRT start/end), `4079-0.0`/`4080-0.0` (diastolic/systolic BP), `20116-0.0` (smoking), `21001-0.0` (BMI), and cardiac MRI fields `24105-2.0`/`24105-3.0` (LV myocardial mass), `24110-2.0`/`24110-3.0` (LA maximum volume), `24113-2.0`/`24113-3.0` (LA ejection fraction).
- Population table: `[private-path]/ukb_ce68812c3a782e09.parquet`, source `ukb_ce68812c3a782e09_parquet`, 502,370 rows. Required columns: `eid`, `31-0.0`, `34-0.0` (year of birth), `21022-0.0` (ethnicity). Join on `eid` only; do not join to Olink or other identifier namespaces.
- Outcomes table: `[private-path]/ukb_e53f1b242ccf9047.parquet`, source `ukb_e53f1b242ccf9047_parquet`, 502,370 rows. Required columns: `eid`, `41270-0.0` (ICD-10 diagnosis), `41280-0.0` (first inpatient diagnosis date), `40000-0.0` (death date), `40001-0.0` (underlying cause of death). Use only non-null values and dates after the assessment; do not treat the array as a complete longitudinal history.

## Variables and estimand
Primary exposure: continuous age at natural menopause, standardized per 5 years; secondary binary early menopause <45 years versus >=45 years, with <40 years as a prespecified subgroup. Primary outcomes: LV myocardial mass and LA maximum volume at the same assessment, normalized by BMI or height if the solver can validate units; LA ejection fraction is secondary. Estimand: adjusted mean difference in outcome per 5-year earlier menopause among women with complete baseline measurements. This is descriptive/associational, not causal.

## Analysis and baseline
Primary baseline: ordinary least squares with restricted cubic splines for age at MRI, BMI, systolic and diastolic BP, smoking, and HRT start/end; cluster robust uncertainty is not appropriate for a single assessment. Report coefficient, 95% CI, missingness, and partial R². Use a complete-case primary analysis and a multiple-imputation sensitivity analysis. The substantive alternative is a penalized multivariate elastic-net model predicting the two primary structural outcomes jointly, with the same covariates and an interaction between menopause age and BMI/BP. It can reveal whether early menopause has a distinct joint structural pattern that the univariate baseline loses, but it cannot identify a mechanism. Compare coefficient stability and held-out standardized prediction error using participant-level 5-fold cross-validation; no GPU is needed. A mechanistic mediation claim is deferred because no reliable longitudinal exposure, repeated cardiac measurements, or adjudicated treatment indication is available.

## Falsification and interpretation
Supportive: the direction is consistent for LV mass and LA volume, the interaction is not driven by a single covariate, and the association remains in the repeat-measurement subset with uncertainty reported. Adverse: estimates are null or reverse after BP/HRT adjustment, or are confined to one MRI instance/one outcome; interpret as no evidence for a robust structural association. Inconclusive: wide CIs, separation, or missingness prevent resolution; do not call it negative. A positive result does not establish that menopause causes remodeling; residual confounding, selection into cardiac MRI, HRT, smoking, and common cardiovascular risk remain. Clinical adjudication and external replication would be required for causal or treatment claims.

## Observed feasibility and limitations
A read-only column-projection check found 165,321 rows with field 3581, 1083 rows with any cardiac MRI field, and 175 rows with both valid menopause age and cardiac MRI; the 175-row subset has menopause ages 31–58 years. This is too small for precise causal adjustment or reliable event analysis. The experiment must report this limitation and treat any effect as exploratory. Event counts and complete medication/indication data are unavailable or insufficient for the proposed clinical endpoint extension. The three demonstration methods were considered: Delphi-style sequence learning is deferred because only one cardiac assessment is usable; ALADYNOULLI-style latent longitudinal modeling is deferred because repeated imaging is sparse; Oncoformer-style multimodal learning is not applicable because no imaging payload is available. A simple baseline plus penalized multivariate alternative is the smallest scientifically useful comparison.

## Actual deliverable
Fit the baseline and alternative on the 175 eligible women, produce cohort flow, covariate balance/missingness, adjusted coefficients with uncertainty, cross-validation comparison, and a conclusion classified as supportive, adverse, or inconclusive. No full-study result is claimed in this proposal.

The strongest existing evidence supports an observational association between early menopause and cardiovascular events, but does not establish a causal hormonal mechanism; a recent MR review found no significant causal association for coronary heart disease or stroke. The unresolved claim here is narrower: whether the association is present in measured LV/LA structure and persists after measured cardiovascular load adjustment.

## Population and time
Use UKB `ukb672073` participants with sex=2, field 2724=1 (had natural menopause), and positive field 3581 (age at last menstrual period). Restrict to baseline assessment instance 0 for the primary cross-sectional association; do not use instance 3 as follow-up because the available MRI instance timing is not sufficient to establish a prospective change. Follow-up events are secondary and exploratory only. The assessment date is field 53-0.0; field 53-1.0 is available for a repeat-measurement sensitivity analysis but only 20,343 rows have it in the completed subset.

## Exact data bindings
All joins use `eid` within the `ukb672073` identifier namespace. Source snapshot is `ukb-completed-subset-20261002`.

Required columns: `eid`, `31-0.0` (sex), `53-0.0`/`53-1.0` (assessment dates), `2724-0.0` (had menopause), `3581-0.0` (age at menopause), `3536-0.0`/`3546-0.0` (HRT start/end), `4079-0.0`/`4080-0.0` (diastolic/systolic BP), `20116-0.0` (smoking), `21001-0.0` (BMI), and cardiac MRI fields `24105-2.0`/`24105-3.0` (LV myocardial mass), `24110-2.0`/`24110-3.0` (LA maximum volume), `24113-2.0`/`24113-3.0` (LA ejection fraction).

- Outcomes table: `[private-path]/ukb_e53f1b242ccf9047.parquet`, source `ukb_e53f1b242ccf9047_parquet`, 502,370 rows. Required columns: `eid`, `41270-0.0` (ICD-10 diagnosis), `41280-0.0` (first inpatient diagnosis date), `40000-0.0` (death date), `40001-0.0` (underlying cause of death). Use only non-null values and dates after the assessment; do not treat the array as a complete longitudinal history.

## Variables and estimand
Primary exposure: continuous age at natural menopause, standardized per 5 years; secondary binary early menopause <45 years versus >=45 years, with <40 years as a prespecified subgroup. Primary outcomes: LV myocardial mass and LA maximum volume at the same assessment, normalized by BMI or height if the solver can validate units; LA ejection fraction is secondary. Estimand: adjusted mean difference in outcome per 5-year earlier menopause among women with complete baseline measurements. This is descriptive/associational, not causal.

## Analysis and baseline
Primary baseline: ordinary least squares with restricted cubic splines for age at MRI, BMI, systolic and diastolic BP, smoking, and HRT start/end; cluster robust uncertainty is not appropriate for a single assessment. Report coefficient, 95% CI, missingness, and partial R². Use a complete-case primary analysis and a multiple-imputation sensitivity analysis. The substantive alternative is a penalized multivariate elastic-net model predicting the two primary structural outcomes jointly, with the same covariates and an interaction between menopause age and BMI/BP. It can reveal whether early menopause has a distinct joint structural pattern that the univariate baseline loses, but it cannot identify a mechanism. Compare coefficient stability and held-out standardized prediction error using participant-level 5-fold cross-validation; no GPU is needed. A mechanistic mediation claim is deferred because no reliable longitudinal exposure, repeated cardiac measurements, or adjudicated treatment indication is available.

## Falsification and interpretation
Supportive: the direction is consistent for LV mass and LA volume, the interaction is not driven by a single covariate, and the association remains in the repeat-measurement subset with uncertainty reported. Adverse: estimates are null or reverse after BP/HRT adjustment, or are confined to one MRI instance/one outcome; interpret as no evidence for a robust structural association. Inconclusive: wide CIs, separation, or missingness prevent resolution; do not call it negative. A positive result does not establish that menopause causes remodeling; residual confounding, selection into cardiac MRI, HRT, smoking, and common cardiovascular risk remain. Clinical adjudication and external replication would be required for causal or treatment claims.

## Observed feasibility and limitations
A read-only column-projection check found 165,321 rows with field 3581, 1083 rows with any cardiac MRI field, and 175 rows with both valid menopause age and cardiac MRI; the 175-row subset has menopause ages 31–58 years. This is too small for precise causal adjustment or reliable event analysis. The experiment must report this limitation and treat any effect as exploratory. Event counts and complete medication/indication data are unavailable or insufficient for the proposed clinical endpoint extension. The three demonstration methods were considered: Delphi-style sequence learning is deferred because only one cardiac assessment is usable; ALADYNOULLI-style latent longitudinal modeling is deferred because repeated imaging is sparse; Oncoformer-style multimodal learning is not applicable because no imaging payload is available. A simple baseline plus penalized multivariate alternative is the smallest scientifically useful comparison.

## Actual deliverable
Fit the baseline and alternative on the 175 eligible women, produce cohort flow, covariate balance/missingness, adjusted coefficients with uncertainty, cross-validation comparison, and a conclusion classified as supportive, adverse, or inconclusive. No full-study result is claimed in this proposal.
